types.name: ConnectorEntityListFilterInput
types.description:
Narrows the entities of one namespace. `previewConnectorEntities` (as `list.filter`) is the searchable listing; `listConnectorEntities` rejects a non-blank `searchQuery` with `UNIMPLEMENTED`.

| Field | `listConnectorEntities` | `previewConnectorEntities` |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | `eq` / `in` | `eq` / `in` |
| `refId`, `mappingKey` | `eq` / `in` | ignored; use `searchQuery` |
| `mergingState` | the first of `eq`, `in`, `ne` that is set | `eq`, `in` and `ne` together, against the state the entity would have after this save |
| `lastChangeDate` | every operator set, so `gte` + `lte` is a closed range; an entity never merged matches no bound | same |
| `lastChangeKind` | the first of `eq`, `in`, `ne` that is set | same |
| `searchQuery` | rejected | the grammar below |

**searchQuery**

Up to three parts, separated by whitespace, in any order, all combined with AND. Canonical order:

```text
#tags gridv1:TOKEN free text
```

**Free text**

- Split on whitespace; every word must appear, as a case-insensitive substring, somewhere in the entity. Word order does not matter.
- Searched: `refId`, the `exactType` and `baseType` names, every `context` value, and every field value of any type (displayed, default and saved), including an entity reference's readable parts.
- Platform ids (`id`, `mappedId`, `mappingKey`, `legacyMappingKey`, and the ids inside an entity reference) match only a word of 8 or more characters: a pasted id finds its entity, a short word such as `2` never matches every entity through a shared id prefix.
- Never searched: `sourceType`, context keys starting with `__`, field slugs, labels and `options`, boolean values, and platform state such as `mergingState` (use the hashtags).

**Hashtags**

Case-insensitive and whitespace-bounded; several are combined with AND. Each keeps the entities carrying that tag in `context.__preview.tags`:

- `#selected`: selected after this save.
- `#added`: this save adds it to the graph.
- `#updated`: already in the graph, and its values change (by a user, a rule, or the source system since its last merge).
- `#deleted`: a user or a rule unselected it, so this save deletes it from the graph; never a missing entity.
- `#missing`: merged, but the source system no longer reports it, so every save deletes it; never tagged `deleted`.
- `#firstSeen`: first imported after the namespace's last save, selected or not; none until the namespace has been saved or merged once.
- `#unresolved`: added or updated, with an entity reference pointing at nothing in the graph. It runs the graph check: if the check cannot complete, the request fails with `ABORTED` (retry) or `RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED` (too many references) instead of returning an empty page.

Any other `#word`, and a tag glued to another word (`abc#added`), is free text.

**Grid token**

A column filter and sort, at most one per query: `gridv1:` followed by the unpadded base64url encoding of this JSON (MUI X DataGrid's filter and sort models; other keys are ignored, both models are optional):

```json
{
  "filterModel": {
    "items": [{ "field": "floor", "operator": ">=", "value": 2 }],
    "logicOperator": "and"
  },
  "sortModel": [{ "field": "name", "sort": "asc" }]
}
```

- `logicOperator` is `and` (the default) or `or`, over a flat list of items. `sort` is `asc`, `desc`, or `null` (ignored).
- `field` is a field slug, `@` followed by a context key (non-string values compare as their JSON), or one of the reserved keys `refId`, `mappingKey`, `mappedId`, `legacyMappingKey`. A field slug the namespace does not declare is ignored; a context key starting with `__` is rejected.
- Columns compare as numbers (`FLOOR_LEVEL` fields), by presence only (`ENTITY_REF` fields, whose names are resolved client-side; not sortable), or as text (every other field and key). Operators:

```text
operator                                  text  number  entity reference
contains, doesNotContain                  yes   -       -
equals, =, is / doesNotEqual, !=, not     yes   yes     -
startsWith, endsWith                      yes   -       -
isEmpty, isNotEmpty                       yes   yes     yes
isAnyOf (value is an array)               yes   yes     -
>, >=, <, <=                              -     yes     -
```

- Values compare against the displayed value (after rules and unsaved edits). Text equality and `isAnyOf` ignore case and accents; `contains`, `startsWith` and `endsWith` ignore case only. Blank text counts as empty. An item with no usable value (missing, blank, `NaN`, an empty array) is ignored.
- Sort keys apply in order: natural order ("Room 2" before "Room 10"), case-insensitive, empty values last in both directions, ties broken by entity `id`.
- Filters and sorts the listing before pagination; never changes the counts.
- Limits, counted before ignored fields are dropped: 50 filter items, 200 `isAnyOf` values summed over the whole query, 10 sort keys, and a 32 KiB encoded payload.
- A second token, an unknown `gridvN` version, a payload that is not base64url JSON of this shape, an unknown operator, an operator the column cannot take, a sort on an entity reference, or a limit exceeded fails with `INVALID_ARGUMENT` and a message starting `Invalid grid query:`.

**Example**

For a namespace with fields `floor` (`FLOOR_LEVEL`), `building` (`ENTITY_REF`) and `name` (`NAME`): entities this save adds, on floor 2 or above, whose `department` context is IT or Facilities, with a building set, containing "lobby", sorted by name.

```text
#added gridv1: lobby
```

The token decodes to:

```json
{
  "filterModel": {
    "items": [
      { "field": "floor", "operator": ">=", "value": 2 },
      { "field": "@department", "operator": "isAnyOf", "value": ["IT", "Facilities"] },
      { "field": "building", "operator": "isNotEmpty" }
    ],
    "logicOperator": "and"
  },
  "sortModel": [{ "field": "name", "sort": "asc" }]
}
```

types.name: OpenUSDLayer
types.description: A durable, resolvable OpenUSD artifact. Root layers additionally carry the stage metadata - units, up axis, handedness, time-code rate - which is where USD stores it. Runtime stages and prims are deliberately not modelled; a binding resolves in a layer.

fields.name: assetIdentifier
fields.description: The USD asset path the author wrote. Identity, not a location - use contentUrl to fetch the bytes.

fields.name: contentHash
fields.description: Digest of the layer's bytes, "sha256:<64 hex>". Verify downloads against it and key caches on it.

fields.name: contentUrl
fields.description:
A URL the caller can GET to receive exactly the bytes contentHash names. Opaque and
possibly short-lived: do not parse it, persist it, or derive sibling URLs from it -
composition dependencies are found through referencesLayer. Null when Mapped cannot
serve the bytes; never an error. Nullable String so a signed URL can replace the
pass-through later without a schema change.
  
The relationMapping is what pulls the asset identifier into the projection when the
client did not select assetIdentifier - the fix #2949 made for Connector.contributions.
parentField names the VERTEX property, not the GraphQL field: core reads it straight
off the source map (RelationMappingConverter#getSourceFieldValue), which is why
Thing.model maps deviceModelId and not a field Thing has. Hence openUSDAssetIdentifier.

types.name: OpenUSDPrimBinding
types.description: A reified binding from a semantic vertex to one prim address in one layer. It has its own identity because a relationship carries no property bag and the association needs provenance and a validity window. Its properties describe the association - where it points, what it expects to find, whether it may drive pose - never intrinsic prim facts. A binding with hasLODItem edges is a level-of-detail root; an item binding is owned through its root.

fields.name: coordinateFrame

The coordinate-frame registry entry coordinateFrameId names. Null when the binding
names no frame, and null - not an error - when it names one the registry does not
hold: a stale frame id is data, and it must not fail a list of a thousand bindings.

fields.name: lodOverrideIndex

fields.name: lodOverrideMode
fields.description: In USD's spelling - inherited, noOverride, indexedLOD, noLOD or allLOD.

fields.description: The last level-of-detail index at which this binding's prim exists. Absent means every level. A joint's or a wheel's prim is typically authored at level 0 only.

fields.description: What the binding expects to find at primPath, e.g. Xform.
